answer.rationale: Write-path p99 began climbing ~30 minutes after the release went out, making the new build the leading suspect; memory_b1 shows a prior rollback cleared a similar post-release error spike without customer impact, and memory_b6 confirms the release pipeline has surfaced bad builds before. Rollback restores the known-stable build, directly protects customer writes (unlike read-replica routing, which addresses reads only), and is reversible. Verifying b1's archived record confirms the rollback was clean under load before committing the single intervention window. Regional failover and capacity adds treat symptoms without addressing the likely cause; circuit breakers target a partner dependency, not an internal regression. If verification shows b1's rollback caused write loss, I would switch to add_capacity instead.
